en: The Śarabha Upaniṣad
Having renounced everything, the sages resort to that which is the nature of the Self;
that Śārabha, the three-quartered Brahman, remains as the Self alone.
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O Gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O Holy Ones. With firm limbs and bodies, may we praise [you] with hymns of praise.
May we attain that life which is ordained by the gods. May Indra, of far-reaching fame, grant us well-being; may Pūṣan and the Viśvedevas grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are unbroken, grant us well-being;
may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us.
Oṃ. Peace, peace, peace.
Then Paippalāda said to that Brahman: "O Blessed One, among Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, who indeed is the most preeminent one to be meditated upon? Pray, tell us the truth."
To him the Grandfather said: "O Paippalāda, listen to these words;
by him many meritorious deeds have been performed."
By that alone is this Supreme Lord to be attained— He from whose body I was born, whom Hari and the leaders of the gods, including Indra, do not know due to delusion. || 1 ||
To Him who appoints Brahmā as the venerable Lord, the Father, and the Great Ruler,
and who sends forth all the Vedas as the foremost [revelation].
Him indeed as the lord, the father of the deities. || 2 ||
I too [sought refuge] in that worshipful god Viṣṇu, my progenitor,
who at the time of the end withdrew all the worlds.
He alone is the preeminent teacher of all, and he alone is the most excellent;
that Maheśvara of great power, having assumed the formidable form known as Śarabha, slew Nṛsiṃha, the destroyer of the world. (4)
As Hari was carrying him away on his two feet, the lords of the gods followed after him, saying:
"Do not kill the person Viṣṇu; stride forth, for you are great! (5)
Out of compassion, the Lord tore Viṣṇu with his sharp claws;
the great hero Vīrabhadra, clad in skin, came into being.
That one Rudra alone is to be meditated upon for the attainment of all perfections by everyone;
homage be to that Rudra who is the destroyer of the five-faced Brahmā. || 7 ||

Salutations be to that Rudra, who by a spark born from his forehead reduces the entire world to ashes, and having created it again, protects it once more, thus manifesting himself as the independent Lord. 8.
Salutations be to that Rudra, who struck down Kāla with his left foot and then drank the burning Hālāhala poison. || 9 ||
Salutations to that Rudra, who, being exceedingly delighted, gave his discus to him by whom the eye of Viṣṇu was pierced with his left foot. 10.
Salutations be to that Rudra, the hero who, at Dakṣa’s sacrifice, having conquered the hosts of gods, bound Viṣṇu with a serpent-noose. 11.
He who, with his eyes as the moon, sun, and fire, sportively burnt the triple city— Viṣṇu, the Seer—
before whom all the gods attained the state of sacrificial beasts.
Therefore, Paśupati himself became that;
let there be salutation to that Rudra. || 12 ||
He who [is] Viṣṇu, the Fish, the Tortoise, and others, the Boar, the Lion, and Vāmana, the primordial Viṣṇu;
who reduced to ashes Manmatha and Yama, as well as the Lord of the Gods when he was distressed and overwhelmed by fear.
Let there be salutation to that Rudra. || 13 ||
Having praised Maheśvara, the blue-throated one, in this manner and in many ways, they sought his forgiveness for the births,
deaths, old age, and other afflictions arising from the three types of suffering.
The Supreme Lord did not remove various kinds of sufferings. ||14||
Thus entreated by the mantras, the primordial Lord Śaṅkara, the Self of all embodied beings, indeed protected all creatures. || 15 ||
Having praised Maheśāna, who is worthy of praise and beyond the reach of speech and mind, [I praise] that pair of lotus-feet which is sought after even by Viṣṇu. (16)
The omnipresent Lord bestowed his grace upon Viṣṇu, whose body was bowed in devotion,
[Viṣṇu] who knows the bliss of Brahman— of which speech turns back along with the mind, unable to reach it— and who therefore never fears anything. (17)
Smaller than the smallest and greater than the greatest, the Self is hidden in the cave of the heart of this living being.
Free from sorrow, one beholds that Lord, the Greatness, who is beyond ritual action, through the grace of the Creator. 18.

The venerable Maheśa, the primordial God, who is meditated upon in the hearts of Vasiṣṭha, Vyāsa, Vāmadeva, Viriñci, and other preeminent sages, and who is praised by Sanatsujāta, Sanātana, and others—[to him I bow]. (19)
The Lord of the Mountain is the Blessed One— truthful, eternal, the witness of all,
the Great Lord, perpetual bliss, free from conceptual construction, beyond description,
and possessed of inconceivable power.
The ground of the ego-sense is imagined by one's own ignorance. || 20 ||

O observer of noble vows, this illusion causes extreme delusion for both me and Viṣṇu; yet, through meditation upon his lotus feet, it becomes easily crossed over, though it was otherwise difficult to traverse.
Viṣṇu, the source of the entire universe, having become born from a portion of me together with his own parts, protects the whole world.
Everything else perishes in time; therefore, all else is false.
Om! Salutation be to that Great Devourer, to Mahādeva, the wielder of the trident, to Maheśvara, to Mṛḍa, to that Rudra. || 23 ||
Viṣṇu alone is the great being; though one, he exists manifoldly as the abode of all beings.
Pervading the three worlds, the imperishable soul of all beings, the consumer of the universe, enjoys [them]. 24.
May that Viṣṇu be pleased with me, who is offered oblations four times, four times, twice, five times, and again twice.
The offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman;
by him who is absorbed in the yoga of action that is Brahman, Brahman alone is to be attained. 26.
The living beings are the arrows; Hari himself shines eternally within their limbs.
O great sage, this Śarabha is indeed Brahman itself, the direct bestower of liberation. (27)
The gods themselves are deluded by the power of Māyā through notions such as "mine-ness" (mamatā) and the like;
no one is able to describe even a minute fraction of His majesty. (28)

Brahman is higher than the highest; Hari is higher than that which is higher than the highest; indeed, Īśa is higher than that which is higher than the highest; therefore, there is none equal to Him, nor any superior.
Śiva alone is eternal; everything other than him is false. Therefore, abandoning all other deities such as Viṣṇu and the rest who are objects of meditation, [one should worship him].
Śiva alone is always to be meditated upon, the liberator from the entire cycle of worldly existence;
salutation to that Maheśvara, the great devourer. || 31 ||
This great scripture of Paippalāda should not be given to just anyone—
not to an atheist, nor to an ungrateful person, nor to one of evil conduct, nor to one of wicked soul.
To one who is hypocritical, cruel, deceitful, and a speaker of falsehood;
and to one who is firm in vows, deeply devoted, of good conduct, and of excellent character—33.
It should be given to one who is devoted to the guru, self-controlled, peaceful, upright in mind,
devoted to Śiva, and wise regarding the duties of Brahman as they have been declared.
O best of the twice-born, this excellent vow should be given only to one's own devotee who is not ungrateful;
it must never be given to others, but kept secret with great effort.
The twice-born who studies this great scripture of Paippalāda and causes it to be heard becomes liberated from birth and death;
he who knows it attains immortality.
And he goes [to that state];
he becomes liberated from dwelling in a womb;
he is purified from the drinking of liquor.
He becomes purified; he is purified from the theft of gold;
he is purified from the murder of a Brahmin.
He becomes purified from violating the teacher’s bed;
he has studied all the Vedas.
He becomes one who has meditated upon all the gods;
he becomes purified from all major and minor sins.
Therefore, he takes refuge in the Unliberated;
he becomes constantly dear to Śiva;
he attains union with Śiva.
He does not return again, he does not return again;
he becomes Brahman itself.
"Thus spoke the Blessed One as Brahman," so says the Upaniṣad.
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O Gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O Holy Ones. With firm limbs and bodies, may we praise you.
May we attain the life-span ordained by the gods. May Indra, of far-reaching fame, grant us well-being;
may Pūṣan, the all-knowing, grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya, whose wheel is unbroken, grant us well-being;
may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us.
Oṃ! Peace, peace, peace.
Thus ends the Śarabha Upaniṣad.
